text: On the glass case stood a tiger made of papier mâché, which kept nodding its head in a slow and regular way. <break time="0.8s" /> There were also magic mirrors, one of which stretched us long and thin, while another swelled our heads and made our legs vanish. <break time="0.8s" /> While we were laughing at the mirrors, the shopman appeared, a pale man with one ear larger than the other. <break time="0.8s" /> When I asked for a few simple tricks for my boy, he took a glass ball out of his own head and held it out to Gip. <break time="0.8s" /> Gip reached for it, but his hand closed on nothing, and the shopman said calmly, It is in your pocket, and there it was. <break time="0.8s" /> He then took more balls from his elbow and the back of his neck, and he would take no money for them at all. <break time="0.8s" /> He gave me a card that said Genuine Magic Shop, and he said firmly that there was absolutely no deception in his shop. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he smiled at Gip and said that he was the Right Sort of Boy, the only sort that could get through the doorway. <break time="0.8s" /> Just then a little boy outside rattled the door and howled, but it stayed firmly shut, and someone carried him away. <break time="0.8s" /> The door is locked for that sort of child, the shopman explained, and he flicked a few colored sparks from his fingers.
